figure.title: Triage of patients with advanced heart failure and appropriate timing of referral
figure.summary: Flowchart to triage patients with advanced heart failure (HF) showing decision nodes for referral to advanced HF centre, management in local HF service, re-evaluation intervals, and palliative care for patients with very limited life expectancy or poor quality of life.
decision_nodes: Patients with very limited life expectancy and/or poor QOL that may impair follow-up or worsen prognosis after advanced HF therapies -> consider palliative care.
NYHA III–IV despite optimal medical therapy (including ICD/CRT when indicated) vs NYHA class II -> assess for any high-risk characteristics.
If any high-risk characteristics present -> consider referral to or discussion with advanced HF centre.
If no high-risk characteristics -> manage in local HF service with re-evaluation every 3–6 months.

high_risk_characteristics_prompting_refe: >1 admission or unplanned visit to HF clinic within last 12 months
Need for escalating diuretic doses for persistent congestion
Systolic blood pressure (SBP) < 90 mmHg and/or signs of peripheral hypoperfusion
content.management_recommendations_summary: In patients with advanced HF, pharmacological therapy and short-term mechanical circulatory support (MCS) may be needed until implantation of long-term MCS or heart transplantation becomes available. Patients managed locally should be re-evaluated every 3–6 months; those with high-risk features should be referred to or discussed with an advanced HF centre. Palliative care is appropriate for patients with very limited life expectancy or poor QOL.
